author: 64cf7168c6edd65797781320
chapter_outcomes: Students will be able to eliminate incorrect options during the first playback of a recording and confirm their final answer during the replay.
Students will be able to underline key words during the allotted reading time to spot answers more efficiently when the audio plays.
Students will be able to construct mental sequences of events to make finding the final answer easier for visual multiple-choice questions.
Students will be able to identify specific conditions in a question, such as "now" or "yesterday," to select the correct option when all visual choices are mentioned in the recording.
Students will be able to deduce the correct answer by identifying the specific option that characters explicitly agree upon.
Students will be able to demonstrate understanding of implicit meanings by assuming all options are correct and using audio evidence to systematically eliminate the wrong ones.
Students will be able to evaluate indirect statements by paying attention to narrowing words like "last," "first," and "now".
Students will be able to analyze short monologues to identify which main idea a speaker talks about most or expresses a strong opinion on.
Students will be able to recognize confirming phrases in interviews, such as "nothing beats it for me," to connect a speaker's feelings to the correct multiple-choice option.
Students will be able to utilize the last sentence or phrase of an audio segment before the next question as a critical clue to narrow down their answer.
Students will be able to extract specific spoken data regarding common exam topics, including price, time, location, reasons, opinions, and numbers.
Students will be able to evaluate spoken English across different accents (British, American, and Australian) by listening for possible synonyms of the written options rather than exact word matches.
